1.text: The burden which the prophet Ambacum saw.

2.text: How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and thou wilt not hearken? [how long] shall I cry out to thee being injured, and thou wilt not save?
2.raw_text: How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and thou wilt not hearken? [how long] shall I cry out to thee being injured, and thou wilt not save?

3.text: Wherefore hast thou shewn me troubles and griefs to look upon, misery and ungodliness? judgment is before me, and the judge receives a reward.
3.raw_text: Wherefore hast thou shewn me troubles and griefs to look upon, misery and ungodliness? judgment is before me, and the judge receives a reward.

4.text: Therefore the law is frustrated, and judgment proceeds not effectually, for the ungodly [man] prevails over the just; therefore perverse judgment will proceed.
4.raw_text: Therefore the law is frustrated, and judgment proceeds not effectually, for the ungodly [man] prevails over the just; therefore perverse judgment will proceed.

5.text: Behold, ye despisers, and look, and wonder marvellously, and vanish: for I work a work in your days, which ye will in no wise believe, though a man declare [it to you].
5.raw_text: Behold, ye despisers, and look, and wonder marvellously, and vanish: for I work a work in your days, which ye will in no wise believe, though a man declare [it to you].

6.text: Wherefore, behold, I stir up the Chaldeans, the bitter and hasty nation, that walks upon the breadth of the earth, to inherit tabernacles not his own.
6.raw_text: Wherefore, behold, I stir up the Chaldeans, the bitter and hasty nation, that walks upon the breadth of the earth, to inherit tabernacles not his own.

7.text: He is terrible and famous; his judgment shall proceed of himself, and his dignity shall come out of himself.
7.raw_text: He is terrible and famous; his judgment shall proceed of himself, and his dignity shall come out of himself.

8.text: And his horses shall bound [more swiftly] than leopards, and [they are] fiercer than the wolves of Arabia: and his horsemen shall ride forth, and shall rush from far; and they shall fly as an eagle hasting to eat.

9.text: Destruction shall come upon ungodly men, resisting with their adverse front, and he shall gather the captivity as the sand.
9.raw_text: Destruction shall come upon ungodly men, resisting with their adverse front, and he shall gather the captivity as the sand.

10.text: And he shall be at his ease with kings, and princes are his toys, and he shall mock at every strong-hold, and shall cast a mound, and take possession of it.
10.raw_text: And he shall be at his ease with kings, and princes are his toys, and he shall mock at every strong-hold, and shall cast a mound, and take possession of it.

11.text: Then shall he change his spirit, and he shall pass through, and make an atonement, [saying], This strength [belongs] to my god.
11.raw_text: Then shall he change his spirit, and he shall pass through, and make an atonement, [saying], This strength [belongs] to my god.

12.text: [Art] not thou from the beginning, O Lord God, my Holy One? and surely we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast established it for judgment, and he has formed me to chasten [with] his correction.

13.text: [His] eye is too pure to behold evil [doings], and to look upon grievous afflictions: wherefore dost thou look upon despisers? wilt thou be silent when the ungodly swallows up the just?

14.text: And wilt thou make men as the fishes of the sea, and as the reptiles which have no guide?
14.raw_text: And wilt thou make men as the fishes of the sea, and as the reptiles which have no guide?

15.text: He has brought up destruction with a hook, and drawn one with a casting net, and caught another in his drags: therefore shall his heart rejoice and be glad.

16.text: Therefore will he sacrifice to his drag, and burn incense to his casting-net, because by them he has made his portion fat, and his meats choice.
16.raw_text: Therefore will he sacrifice to his drag, and burn incense to his casting-net, because by them he has made his portion fat, and his meats choice.

17.text: Therefore will he cast his net, and will not spare to slay the nations continually.

1.text: I will stand upon my watch, and mount upon the rock, and watch to see what he will say by me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.
1.raw_text: I will stand upon my watch, and mount upon the rock, and watch to see what he will say by me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.

2.text: And the Lord answered me and said, Write the vision, and [that] plainly on a tablet, that he that reads it may run.
2.raw_text: And the Lord answered me and said, Write the vision, and [that] plainly on a tablet, that he that reads it may run.

3.text: For the vision [is] yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.
3.raw_text: For the vision [is] yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

4.text: If he should draw back, my soul has no pleasure in him: but the just shall live by my faith.
4.raw_text: If he should draw back, my soul has no pleasure in him: but the just shall live by my faith.

5.text: But the arrogant man and the scorner, the boastful man, shall not finish anything; who has enlarged his desire as the grave, and like death he is never satisfied, and he will gather to himself all the nations, and will receive to himself all the peoples.

6.text: Shall not all these take up a parable against him? and a proverb to tell against him? and they shall say, Woe to him that multiplies to himself the possessions which are not his! how long? and who heavily loads his yoke.

7.text: For suddenly there shall arise up those that bite him, and they that plot against thee shall awake, and thou shalt be a plunder to them.

8.text: Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the nations that are left shall spoil [thee], because of the blood of men, and the sins of the land and city, and of all that dwell in it.

9.text: Woe to him that covets an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evils.
9.raw_text: Woe to him that covets an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evils.

10.text: Thou hast devised shame to thy house, thou hast utterly destroyed many nations, and thy soul has sinned.
10.raw_text: Thou hast devised shame to thy house, thou hast utterly destroyed many nations, and thy soul has sinned.

11.text: For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beetle out of the timber shall speak.
11.raw_text: For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beetle out of the timber shall speak.

12.text: Woe to him that builds a city with blood, and establishes a city by unrighteousness.
12.raw_text: Woe to him that builds a city with blood, and establishes a city by unrighteousness.

13.text: Are not these things of the Lord Almighty? surely many people have been exhausted in the fire, and many nations have fainted.

14.text: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord; it shall cover them as water.
14.raw_text: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord; it shall cover them as water.

15.text: Woe to him that gives his neighbour to drink the thick lees [of wine], and intoxicates [him], that he may look upon their secret parts.
15.raw_text: Woe to him that gives his neighbour to drink the thick lees [of wine], and intoxicates [him], that he may look upon their secret parts.

16.text: Drink thou also [thy] fill of disgrace instead of glory: shake, O heart, and quake, the cup of the right hand of the Lord has come round upon thee, and dishonour has gathered upon thy glory.

17.text: For the ungodliness of Libanus shall cover thee, and distress because of wild beasts shall dismay thee, because of the blood of men, and the sins of the land and city, and of all that dwell in it.

18.text: What profits it the graven image, that they have graven it? [one] has made it a molten work, a false image; for the maker has trusted in his work, to make dumb idols.

19.text: Woe to him that says to the wood, Awake, arise; and to the stone, Be thou exalted! whereas it is an image, and this is a casting of gold and silver, and there is no breath in it.

20.text: But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth fear before him.

1.text: A Prayer of the Prophet Ambacum, with a Song.

2.text: O Lord, I have heard thy report, and was afraid: I considered thy works, and was amazed: thou shalt be known between the two living creatures, thou shalt be acknowledged when the years draw nigh; thou shalt be manifested when the time is come; when my soul is troubled, thou wilt in wrath remember mercy.

3.text: God shall come from Thæman, and the Holy One from the dark shady mount Pharan. Pause.
